statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC eServices Portal – Companies and Intellectual Property Commission Name Reservation Service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed names must be in plain Latin alphabet or standard transliterated form; names in any of the 11 official languages are permitted; names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters to permit proper registry search and conflict detection. The name must be intelligible, not misleading, and must not contain unusual characters or symbols beyond generally acceptable orthographic conventions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where a name is refused, the applicant may file a written administrative objection through the CIPC eServices portal within 20 business days of the rejection notice, providing reasons why the proposed name satisfies section 23 of the Companies Act 2008. CIPC is required to issue a reconsideration decision within 10 business days. If still unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal to the Companies Tribunal under section 191 of the Companies Act 2008. A name reservation may be extended once through CIPC eServices prior to expiry, upon payment of the applicable extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are accepted for general administrative registered address purposes in South Africa, but for ISIC 4322 cryogenic stainless steel pipe welding and insulation contracting at an LNG receiving terminal, the applicable construction and energy infrastructure licensing regime, including local municipality works registration and EPC client safety and quality audits, requires an operational physical office with project execution capabilities. A stand-alone virtual office is unlikely to satisfy commercial substance expectations for trade licensing and permitting.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High; quantified at 70% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the Department of Employment and Labour, CIPC, South African Revenue Service (SARS), or the local municipality within the first 12 months of active operations due to critical energy infrastructure exposure, statutory health and safety registration, and public-interest licensing thresholds.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; Sections 13 (incorporation), 14 (registration), 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 19 (legal capacity) and Regulation 14 of the Companies Regulations, 2011.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) — CIPC e-Services online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MoI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Proprietary Limited Company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; authorized share capital is derived from the MoI; shares may be issued for nil or nominal consideration, subject to the board's solvency and liquidity test. No government escrow account is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers listed in the MoI subscribe for the initial Share Capital as set forth in Schedule A, each allotment accepted at par, and the Directors are authorized to issue share certificates accordingly. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company is at [address to be inserted], Republic of South Africa, and that a certified lease or consent deed be affixed to the statutory records. RESOLVED FURTHER, that officers are appointed with immediate effect: [Director] as Managing Director, [Director] as Financial Director, and [Name] as Company Secretary, empowered to open bank accounts, appoint auditors, and file all statutory returns with CIPC and SARS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Company Name at CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to CIPC e-Services, complete the free name search, then file the Notice of Reservation of Name (CoR 9.1). Pay the prescribed fee (~ZAR 50; approximately USD 3) by debit card. Wait for the automated verification. Once reserved, the name is held for 60 days (renewable once) during which the incorporation must be filed.
required_dossiers: CoR 9.1 Notice of Reservation of Name
Certified copy of incorporator ID or passport
Name search report printout
Proof of name reservation fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC objects to or queries the name, the applicant may submit a revised CoR 9.1 free of charge within 20 business days or file a written substantive reply to the CIPC Corporate Legal Unit addressing likelihood of confusion or offensiveness per Companies Act s 11.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Contractual drafting by an accredited incorporator or attorney, executed before a commissioner of oaths
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MoI specifying the private company restrictions (no public offer, pre-emptive rights, board quorum and authority thresholds), issuance of no-par shares in one or more classes, incorporation and audit clauses. Prepare CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) and, if desired, CoR 14.2A (SARS/Tax onboarding). Execute the MoI by each incorporator, and the CoR 14.1 by a founder director. Affix original signatures and notarially certify foreign passports when non-resident incorporators are used.
required_dossiers: MoI in the prescribed CIPC format (signed, PDF)
CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation (signed)
CoR 14.2A Taxpayer registration application (optional)
Certified IDs or passports of incorporators, directors and auditor (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar identifies a defect in the MoI or CoR 14.1, the incorporator has 20 business days under Regulation 14.5 to cure the filing; the application is void only if the Registrar issues a formal defective notice and no cure is made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement of Incorporation with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed CoR 14.1 and MoI as searchable PDFs into the CIPC e-Services 'Register a Company' transaction. Pay the statutory incorporation fee (ZAR 175; approximately USD 9) online. Enter the directors' and incorporators' details (full names, dates of birth, ID numbers, postal address). Submit the transaction and take note of the application reference number; the system automatically generates the CoR 14.3 Certificate of Incorporation upon successful registration on the CIPC data key and the Companies Register.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.1 (signed PDF)
MoI (signed PDF)
Certified ID copies of each director
Electronic payment receipt for ZAR 175
Consent of auditor (if audit is mandated in the MoI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queued for manual verification or rejected, the applicant shall respond to the verification questionnaire via e-Services within 20 business days, attach any additional sworn translations or authorizations, and escalate through the CIPC Contact Centre (010 003 0003); re-lodgement is free within 30 days of a rejection due to systems error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and SARS Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (issue of Certificate) and South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download CoR 14.3 (Certificate of Incorporation) from the CIPC e-Services case file. Immediately register on SARS eFiling: complete the documents and payments system to obtain a Notified Tax Number (income tax), register for VAT (compulsory where the annual turnover threshold of ZAR 1 million is exceeded), PAYE, UIF and SDL (skills development levy) as an employer. Obtain a SARS Letter of Segmentation confirming the tax registration.
required_dossiers: CoR 14.3 Certificate of Incorporation
CoR 14.2A Tax registration or SARS eFiling CAC01 registration
Bank confirmation details for refunds (Form A)
Certified copy of MoI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS places a tax registration block or queries the economic substance of a newly registered (Pty) Ltd, submit a solvency declaration and control-chain documentation within 21 days, or appeal under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 s 105, after which the tax number is issued by the SARS Large Business Centre.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Governance and Employer Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (annual returns), Compensation Fund (CF) of the Department of Employment and Labour, UIF/DOL and the Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to issue share certificates and approve minutes; appoint an auditor or independent review practitioner if the MoI so requires; file the Annual Return (CoR 14.2) with CIPC and, where applicable, the Notice of Beneficial Ownership (CoR 44.1) under the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024; register the company as an employer with the Compensation Fund (COIDA form) and the Unemployment Insurance Fund; as a construction contractor, register with the CIDB for a Contractor Grading Determination and submit the Health and Safety Plan required under the Construction Regulations 2014.
required_dossiers: Board minutes of the first meeting and share certificates
CoR 14.2 Annual Return filing (first year)
CoR 44.1 Notice of Beneficial Ownership
COIDA registration form and payment proof
CIDB grading application (determination form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Compensation Fund rejects the employer registration or CIDB grading, correct the payroll derivation (Return of Earnings) and re-submit within 21 days; if CIPC strikes the company off for failure to file annual returns, apply to CIPC for restoration under s 82 of the Companies Act with payment of the reinstatement fee and outstanding returns.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) in conjunction with the Department of Employment and Labour (Chief Directorate: Occupational Health and Safety), the South African Qualification and Certification Committee (SAQCC-Gas), and — for gas transmission pipelines — the National Energy Regulator of South Africa (NERSA) as licensee of the terminal operator
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CIDB Contractor Grading Certificate (GB/GBP classes) and SAQCC Authorised Gas Installer Registration for cryogenic piping works, supported by a DOL Letter of Good Standing (COIDA) and SAQCC assessment compliance certificates for welders and pressure equipment

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) — National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998 (NEMA) and the EIA Regulations 2014 (GNR 982/983/984/985)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Scoping and Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) under Listing Notice 2 for the LNG receiving terminal facility (gas storage and processing is a listed activity); the subsidiary cryogenic piping lay-down and welding workshop triggers a Basic Assessment under Listing Notice 1 Activity 27. The construction company is not the license holder of the terminal EIA authorisation, but must contractually comply with the authorised environmental conditions and train all SHE staff on the approved Environmental Management Programme (EMPr).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: National Water Act 36 of 1998, General Authorisation (GN 665) limits of pH 5.5-9.5 and oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L before any discharge; Air: Atmospheric Emission License thresholds under the NEM: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 for VOCs (stationary tanks) typically set at < 2000 tpa; Welding fume personal exposure limit: 5 mg/m³ (8-hour TWA) as per OHSA and SA health exposure guidelines; Waste: triple-rinse and manifest all waste paints, thinners and contaminated abrasive to an approved NEM:WA registered waste disposal site, retaining disposal certificates for 5 years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: Fire compliance certificate under the National Building Regulations (SANS 10400) issued by the Local Fire Authority for the welding and insulation workshop, with gaseous fire suppression in the torch-out and electrical rooms. Structural: Certificate of stability and load inspection report signed by a registered professional engineer for the lay-down yard, covered fabrication bays, and the installed cryogenic pipe-racks at the terminal interface. Occupational: COIDA Letter of Good Standing from the Department of Employment and Labour under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act 130 of 1993, together with health surveillance certificates for welders exposed to chromium and nickel fumes, HAZMAT storage approval for argon and nitrogen cylinders, and a Major Hazardous Installation (MHI) risk assessment under s 17 of the OHSA for any on-site aggregated LNG inventory exceeding 10 000 kg.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via the SARS eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za); corporate registration with the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) is a prerequisite for domestic entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident or newly formed foreign-owned entities must first register with the CIPC as a private company (Pty) Ltd or external company, obtain a company registration number, then apply to SARS for an Income Tax Reference Number using a COR14/NAT01 form or through eFiling. VAT registration is separately effected via VAT101 (compulsory) or VAT201 (voluntary) forms. All registrations require certified proof of identity, memorandum of incorporation, proof of registered office, and, for non-residents, a Section 10(1)(h) agent appointment or local SARS-appointed representative. External companies deriving taxable supplies from South Africa are also required to register for VAT where turnover exceeds the threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A proprietary limited company is a domestic taxable entity subject to the 27% corporate income tax rate (for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023) on worldwide income from a South African source, with controlled foreign company attribution under Section 9D of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962. It is not eligible for passthrough treatment; a territorial scope does not apply to resident companies; no tax-exempt zone applies outside the SEZ/industrial policy framework.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Relevant elections include: VAT grouping under Section 50 of the VAT Act 89 of 1991 (joint registration for resident group companies); export contracting election under Section 11(2)(q) for taxable services supplied to non-residents; negligible-value supply and deemed-supply elections; prepayment and other timing elections under the Second Schedule to the Income Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch adjustments apply mandatorily under Sections 23F-23M for hybrid financial instruments and hybrid entities, with no revenue-protective election available to ignore the anti-avoidance provisions of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration at ZAR 1,000,000 actual or reasonably expected annual taxable turnover of taxable supplies (Section 23(1)); voluntary registration available from ZAR 50,000 of qualifying turnover (Section 25(1)); foreign businesses making taxable supplies in South Africa may be required to register irrespective of threshold where the liability arises from CIPC external-company status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A real-time fiscal clearance (digital stamping) mandate is NOT yet operational in South Africa. SARS mandates electronic filing and payment via eFiling and offers pre-populated monthly/periodical VAT declarations. SARS generally accepts electronic tax invoices provided they satisfy all Section 20 content and integrity requirements; the SARS Modernization Program is progressing towards a centralized digital e-invoicing exchange, but no live real-time clearance or cryptographic stamping obligation applies currently. For construction/cryogenic piping supplies to a bonded LNG terminal, a fully itemized VAT invoice with a branch VAT number, if applicable, remains mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act for movable goods exported by the supplier outside South Africa; where goods are removed to a non-resident under Section 11(1)(b) (supply to non-resident purchasers) the supplier must obtain and retain documentary proof of export within the prescribed period. Services are zero-rated under Sections 11(2)(k), (l), and (q) for offshore services delivered to non-residents. All zero-rating claims require evidence that the goods or services physically left or were performed outside South Africa; for LNG terminal cryogenic piping, the installation services performed at an operating LNG jetty within South Africa may remain standard-rated unless covered by Section 11(2)(l) or (q) treated as services to a non-resident in respect of movable property situated outside the Republic; direct export of fabricated pipe spools and skid assemblies qualifies for 0%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 on the SARS Customs Automated System showing matching declarations)
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or Road Consignment Note evidencing physical dispatch from South Africa
Commercial Invoice signed by the supplier and accepted by the non-resident buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT proof of receipt of the export purchase price in the exporting entity's South African bank account
Packing list and, for cryogenic piping, the welding/NDT certificate and material test certificates evidencing the offshore-destined goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS auditors apply heightened scrutiny to zero-rated export claims, requiring the exporter to produce the prescribed proof of export within 90 days after the date of supply (Section 11(1)(a) proviso); failure to do so triggers a VAT chargeback to standard rate on the supply. Any false or fraudulent zero-rating declaration attracts an understatement penalty ranging from 10% (substantial understatement) to 150% (intentional tax evasion) of the shortfall under Section 222 of the Tax Administration Act, plus interest under Section 187, a possible 200% additional tax for material fraud under the VAT Act, and criminal prosecution under Section 58A and 59 with fines and imprisonment. Misappropriated export VAT refunds are recoverable by supplementary assessment within 5 years from the date of assessment, or 5 years from the assessment date if fraud, misrepresentation, or non-disclosure is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), under the Currency and Exchanges Act No. 9 of 1933; exchange-control administration is delegated to Authorized Dealers (tier-1 commercial banks) which validate all cross-border flows and perform BoP/EMP reporting on behalf of SARB FinSurv.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is fully convertible for current-account transactions (trade in goods/services, contract advances, royalties, interest, dividends) provided payment instructions are routed through an Authorized Dealer with full supporting documentation. The capital account is controlled but liberalised for inward FDI: non-resident equity subscriptions into a (Pty) Ltd require no prior SARB approval and are processed by the Authorized Dealer as a standard capital-event with BoP coding. Outward investments by a SA-resident entity require prior FinSurv approval unless a specific dispensation applies; therefore the LNG piping contractor must route all capital outflows (shareholder loans, guarantees, acquisitions) via the Authorized Dealer and obtain prior approval where the amount or tenor exceeds de-minimis limits. Profit remittance hurdles are limited: dividends may be remitted to non-resident shareholders upon declaration, subject to a 20% Dividends Withholding Tax (DWT), beneficial-ownership register compliance, and bank EMP reporting; local branch profit remittance/easements are not applicable because the entity is a standalone (Pty) Ltd. Service fees received from the LNG EPC (head contractor) qualify as current-account receipts and are freely convertible, provided a SARS-compliant invoice, the underlying contract, and a valid tax clearance status accompany the receipt.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory repatriation rule: all export and service-fee proceeds must be received into South Africa within 180 days from the date of export (goods) or from the invoice/service-rendering date (services). Mandatory declaration: exports of goods require the SARB Form EX1 (or authorised-dealer electronic equivalent) and the export/import documentation (bill of lading, SAD500 customs entry) must be lodged before shipment. Mandatory conversion: export proceeds must be surrendered to the Authorized Dealer and converted into ZAR immediately upon receipt, unless the exporter maintains an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) with the Authorized Dealer; if retained in an FCA, the funds must be disposed of (sold or applied to approved foreign payments) within 30 days of receipt. For the cryogenic piping contracting business, inbound USD/EUR contract payments from the EPC or LNG terminal owner are treated as services export receipts and are subject to the same 180-day receipt and 30-day disposal/surrender timeline. Non-compliance triggers penalties under the Currency and Exchanges Act, SARB fines, and withdrawal of the Authorized Dealer facility; the treasury must track invoice-aging, receipt dates, and FCA balances daily.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for a primary banking relationship; Medium only as an ancillary payment-composition rail. South Africa does not issue standalone EMI licences to offshore digital financial institutions; non-bank fintech platforms (e.g., Airwallex, Currencycloud, Wise Platform) must clear ZAR through a licensed Authorized Dealer and are subject to FICA, FAIS, and Banks Act outsourcing requirements. No offshore EMI may obtain a direct SAMOS settlement account in ZAR, so all local-currency clearing must settle through a tier-1 bank. Recommended use: fintech rails for FX conversion, cross-border disbursement of subcontractor/equipment payments, and multi-currency visibility, while the (Pty) Ltd retains a tier-1 Authorized Dealer account as the exclusive SARB-reporting treasury node. The EPC contract should therefore name the tier-1 bank account as the sole designated inbound-funds account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under FICA and FIC Guidance Note 7, face-to-face verification is not statutorily absolute where the bank deploys risk-based remote identity verification (non-face-to-face onboarding with biometric liveness checks and electronic verification against DHA/NDRS). However, for a 'Medium_Risk_Enhanced' construction entity with non-resident shareholders, the tier-1 banks in practice will require at least one director (or the sole director and a formally mandated local authorised representative) to attend an in-person or recorded-video compliance interview at the relevant South African branch before account activation. Pure remote account opening is technically permissible after the FIC Amendment Act 2023, but full reliance on it materially raises rejection and prolonged-EDD risk. Mandate: appoint a South African resident director / Financial Director with FATCA/CRS classification and signatory authority, and prepare board resolutions in advance to accelerate the interview phase.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder owning >75% of the (Pty) Ltd with no local director and a short operating history in South Africa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC certificate and Memorandum of Incorporation; Beneficial Ownership Register as filed with CIPC under the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering) Amendment Act 2022; board resolution appointing local authorised signatories; certified passport copies (apostilled); SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN; parent-bank reference; source-of-wealth statement for the share-subscription funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Project-related third-party payments and LC counterparties in cryogenic equipment procurement, generating sanctions-field false positives (EU/UK/US equipment and any Russia/China-origin material) and subcontractor cash-adjacent flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original LNG EPC contract and subcontractor agreements; CIDB contractor grading certificate (valid); ISIC 4322/NAICS 237120 scope description; country-of-origin certificates for stainless steel, valves, insulation; packing lists and HS codes; FICA due-diligence file for each subcontractor; periodic project bank statements and completion certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intragroup funding structured as a shareholder loan, triggering SARB NEP/loan-registration review and potential reclassification of debt as equity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed cross-border loan agreement with arm's-length interest rate and stated tenor; SARS Section 31 transfer-pricing file; loan-registration confirmation issued by the Authorized Dealer to FinSurv; evidence of the entity conducting substantive LNG piping business; audited financial statements of the borrower.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expired or flagged SARS Tax Clearance, or mismatched VAT (zero-rating) treatment on cross-border construction services
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN; two years of audited financial statements; contemporaneous transfer-pricing and VAT zero-rating analysis for export services with underlying EPC contract; proof of DWT and dividend declarations where applicable; SARB BoP codes matching the SARS VAT return.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity-injection protocol: the non-resident shareholder initiates a SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 via correspondent for larger values) to the Authorized Dealer account, with Field 70 remittance information reading 'FDI SHARE SUBSCRIPTION – ZA_PTY_LTD – [CIPC ref] – MOI clause [x]'. The bank routes the credit to a provisional Capital / FDI Escrow sub-account pending presentation of (i) executed shareholder resolution, (ii) share certificate and register, (iii) signed BoP capital declaration. Upon share issuance, funds are released to the operational ZAR account. Prior SARB approval is not required for ordinary-share subscriptions by non-residents; any loan component must be registered with the Authorized Dealer (SARB loan form / NEP) or clearly structured as 'own capital' to avoid loop-structure recharacterisation. Contract-advance (current-account) routing: the LNG EPC or terminal SPV pays via SWIFT MT103, Field 70: 'ADVANCE PAYMENT CONTRACT [ref] – LNG RECEIVING TERMINAL PIPING WORKS'; the (Pty) Ltd issues a SARS-compliant tax invoice; services are zero-rated for VAT; no DWT is withheld on services receipts; the Authorized Dealer will code the receipt as current-account service income for the 180-day surrender clock.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Rail 1 – SWIFT MT103 / MT202 direct transfers: used for international equipment, insulation materials, and offshore subcontractor payments; each instruction requires the underlying invoice, SARS customs entry (SAD500) for goods imports or a service contract for intangibles, and a SARB BoP/EMP code. Rail 2 – Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700): irrevocable, confirmed LC for cryogenic stainless-steel pipe, cryogenic valves, and insulation imports, with Incoterms 2020 and up to 90-day usance tenor; confirmation from a top EU/UK bank is recommended to satisfy supplier comfort and to isolate sanctions risks. Rail 3 – ZAR domestic settlement: local subcontractor and supplier payments via the bank's SAMOS-directed EFT/Faster EFT rails, with full beneficiary FICA/KYC files. Retention money (typically 10% of contract value) is segregated in a Construction Retention Escrow Account held with the same tier-1 bank, released only against engineer's/EPC completion certificates. All outward FX transactions must be transaction-matched and non-speculative; forward cover may be applied against confirmed USD/EUR procurement liabilities.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) in USD/ZAR, EUR/ZAR and GBP/ZAR with tenors up to 12 months for current-account exposures (confirmed EPC revenue and equipment imports); available from Authorized Dealers without prior SARB approval, subject to underlying documentary proof, and strictly prohibited for speculative hedging.

Cross-Currency Swap (CCS) for long-term project finance or non-resident shareholder funding (capital-account hedging of loan principal and interest), permissible with prior FinSurv approval or an Authorized Dealer dispensation where the swap is fully transaction-matched to the funding agreement.

Currency options / zero-cost collars written by the Authorized Dealer over USD/EUR/ZAR, permissible where the premium is expensed and reported as an underlying-trade derivative; tenor and notionals must align with the confirmed construction-receivable or procurement-payable schedule.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): NOT permissible for the South African resident entity in the onshore market; ZAR NDF liquidity exists only offshore via London/New York eligible counterparties. The ZA_PTY_LTD treasury must use onshore deliverable FECs only; if group-level NDF overlay is required, the transaction must be executed by the offshore parent with the SA entity excluded from the NDF confirmation and funding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation; subsequent returns due on each annual anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts administrative penalties per CIPC penalty schedule (ZAR 500 per year, cumulative). Failure to file for 2 consecutive years triggers commencement of deregistration proceedings, leading to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the CIPC Annual Return, within 30 business days after the company’s incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance prevents the issuance of a valid Annual Return and may result in same penalties as the Annual Return, including deregistration risk.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if the company’s public interest score (PIS) is 500 or more, or if the company is listed, a state-owned enterprise, or holds a specific license (e.g., financial services, infrastructure operator). For PIS between 100 and 349, an independent review is required unless the company’s memorandum elects a full audit. PIS below 100 may elect a compilation engagement by an independent accountant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) for public interest companies and entities with fiduciary duties; IFRS for SMEs or South African GAAP for non-public interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a register of beneficial owners (BO) and confirm the accuracy of BO data with CIPC annually as part of the Annual Return. Any change in beneficial ownership must be filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the change and the BO register updated accordingly.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – 750 (ZAR 4,500 – 13,500) depending on service provider and registered office location.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,800 – 8,400 (ZAR 50,000 – 150,000) for a typical private company with medium complexity, subject to scope and risk profiling.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022 (28% for earlier years; Small Business Corporations subject to graduated 0%–27% bands on taxable income up to ZAR 555,600)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays. Preferential deductions: section 12C accelerated wear-and-tear on qualifying plant and machinery (manufacturing assets: 40%/20%/20%/20%); section 12B 100% first-year allowance for renewable-energy assets; section 11D enhanced R&D deduction subject to SARS approval; section 12L energy-efficiency saving allowance (ZAR 0.45/kWh saved); section 24C unexpired-contracts allowance (relevant to LNG piping contractors receiving advance mobilisation payments)
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carry-forward (no statutory expiry) but set-off of an assessed loss is capped at 80% of taxable income for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022; section 20(1A) anti-avoidance may deny loss set-off after substantial shareholding changes without continuity of trade
